subject: gunblade

Category: Weapon.
Subject: gunblade.
Style: Final Fantasy.

spec.name: Revolver Gunblade
spec.description: A Final Fantasy-style gunblade with a bright steel sword blade, a revolver mechanism at the hilt, a barrel along the spine, gold filigree, glowing sapphire and cyan accents, and a hanging lion pendant, standing upright on its pommel.
spec.layout: The weapon stands upright with the blade pointing up (+Y) and the round pommel resting on y = 0. It is a flat-bladed sword, so the blade is thin in X (about 0.04 thick at the base) and wide in Z (0.14). The cutting edge faces the front (+Z) and the spine and barrel face the back (-Z). All axes run through x = 0; the z extent runs from about -0.26 (hammer tail, trigger guard) to +0.14 (guard front). From bottom to top: pommel (y 0-0.09), leather grip (0.09-0.40), crossguard and trigger guard (0.34-0.47), revolver receiver with a side-facing cylinder and rear hammer (0.40-0.70), blade (0.70-1.50), with the barrel riding the spine from y 0.70 to 1.34 (z -0.15..-0.07). The lion pendant hangs on a short chain from a lug on the left guard wing (+X side, x about 0.105) beside the grip, and ends near y 0.17. Final Fantasy look: elegant, slightly exaggerated, polished-steel silhouette with bold gold filigree, dark gunmetal mechanics, and a few glowing sapphire and cyan accents (pommel gem, cylinder jewel, fuller runes, muzzle). Every surface is a flat colour. Engravings, trim, rivets, runes and glints are small separate parts seated on the surface, layered as a dark outline, a main colour and a bright highlight. Light steel on the blade's top, deep steel and gunmetal in the lower mechanism, warm gold for every ornament.

parts.builds: The lower handle from pommel to grip top. (1) Pommel: a faceted lathe cap with a flat base on y=0, radius about 0.05, height 0.09, in gold with goldDeep underside bands, a ring of small gold studs, and a glowing sapphire gem (a small faceted sphere or cone) set in the bottom face and the rounded front. (2) Grip: an 8-sided tube radius 0.03 from y 0.09 to 0.40 in leather, with a diagonal leatherDark cord wrap built as thin rings or a spiral sweep, leatherHi highlight strips on the front, and gold collars (rings) at top and bottom with goldDeep edges. (3) A short sapphire or ruby bead band mid-grip, tiny rivets, and a thin goldPale highlight line on each collar. Everything is centred on x=0, z=0 and stays within x ±0.05 and z ±0.05. No chain here; the charm part hangs beside the grip.
parts.attaches: The pommel base rests on y=0 at pommelBase. The grip top collar meets the receiver's crossguard plate at gripTop.

parts.builds: The revolver mechanism and guard. (1) Frame: a gunmetal housing from y 0.40 to 0.70 with a chunky chamfered front edge, side plates at x ±0.04 with gold trim lines and rivets, and gunmetalHi highlights on the top faces. (2) Crossguard: a gold plate at y 0.40-0.44 spanning x ±0.12 and z -0.06..+0.12, with upswept wing tips and goldDeep underside. On the left wing (+X) is a small ring lug at chainAnchor. Add a filigree scroll motif of small gold parts on the wings. (3) Cylinder on the joint 'cylinder': a chunky 8 to 10-sided drum, axis along X, centred at cylinderCenter, radius 0.085, width 0.07 (x ±0.035). Its two flat faces show six chamber holes in black around a central gold hub (small dark discs plus gold bullet-head rings), and the rim carries fine grooves. A sapphire jewel sits at the hub on the left face (+X). (4) Trigger on the joint 'trigger': a small gold crescent lever hanging from triggerPivot down and back. (5) Trigger guard: a gold sweep loop from guardLoopFront down and back round to guardLoopRear (touching the grip's rear face at z -0.03), about 0.016 thick. (6) Hammer on the joint 'hammer': a gunmetal hooked hammer with a gold spur and a ruby stud at its pivot, pointing back to z about -0.25. (7) Breech block: a gunmetal rear block y 0.60-0.70, z -0.15..-0.07 where the barrel starts, with a gold ring at its top (breechTop). (8) Blade lock collar: a gold and gunmetal band y 0.68-0.70 around the blade root (x ±0.035, z -0.075..+0.095) that the blade passes up through. Colours: gunmetal, gunmetalHi, gold, goldDeep, black, sapphire, ruby, steelDeep.
parts.attaches: Sits on the grip at gripTop and guardPlate. The chain lug is at chainAnchor. The blade root enters at bladeBase through the collar. The barrel starts at breechTop and barrelBase. The cylinder, trigger and hammer ride the joints at their pivot mounts.

parts.builds: The sword blade, thin in X and wide in Z, from y 0.70 to the tip at y 1.50. Build the outline as an extrude (outline in the Z-Y plane, thickness along X) with a straight spine at z -0.07 and an edge at z +0.09 at the base. The edge side swells slightly just above the guard, then tapers with a gentle curve to a clipped diagonal point at bladeTip (z about +0.03, y 1.50). Details: (1) A steelBright main body; a steelShade bevel strip along the cutting edge as a thinner overlapping extrude, with an edgeWhite sharp edge line on the very rim. (2) A recessed fuller groove (steelDeep) along the centre from y 0.80 to 1.38 on both faces (+X and -X) with a thin edgeWhite highlight on its upper rim. (3) Gold inset ricasso block at the blade base (y 0.70-0.82) with goldDeep trim and a small gold emblem (an eight-point star or lion-mane burst) on each face. (4) Glowing glowCyan rune marks (small separate thin extrudes) in a vertical column on the fuller, 5 to 7 runes, with black outline underlays. (5) Three small notches or steps on the edge side near the base (decor ridges in steel and steelShade), and a gold clip band near the tip. (6) A brighter tip highlight (edgeWhite diagonal strip) and a steelDeep spine step line. Keep the blade slim (x ±0.02) so the silhouette is a tall, elegant blade. Colours: steelBright, steel, steelShade, steelDeep, edgeWhite, gold, goldDeep, goldPale, glowCyan, black.
parts.attaches: The root sits inside the receiver's blade collar at bladeBase (y 0.70). The spine face at z -0.07 meets the barrel at spineLine. The tip is the highest point of the model, at y 1.50.

parts.builds: The gun barrel assembly riding the blade's spine, from barrelBase (y 0.70) up to the muzzle (y 1.34), centred on x=0, z=-0.105. (1) Main barrel: an octagonal gunmetal tube radius 0.04 tapering to 0.034, with gunmetalHi top-facing highlight strips and black underside seams. (2) Shroud sleeve: a thicker gunmetal section y 0.72-0.95 with a row of cooling slots (small black inset boxes) and gold band rings at its ends and middle. (3) Spine clamps: 4 steel and gold bracket bands that wrap from barrel to blade spine at intervals, bridging z -0.07 to -0.11. (4) Muzzle: a gold and gunmetal flared muzzle brake with a black bore and a glowCyan ring inside the lip, plus a faint glowing sapphire dot. (5) Front sight: a small gold fin on the back of the muzzle and a rear sight notch near the breech, a thin ruby line, and tiny rivets. (6) Gold filigree scroll or vine small parts running along the barrel's -Z side, and a thin glowCyan line along the shroud. Colours: gunmetal, gunmetalHi, black, gold, goldDeep, goldPale, steel, glowCyan, sapphire, ruby.
parts.attaches: Starts on the receiver breech block at barrelBase and breechTop. Its +Z face touches the blade's spine at spineLine. The muzzle is at the top of the barrel.

parts.builds: The hanging lion pendant, Squall's signature charm, on a chain from the left guard wing lug at chainAnchor (x 0.105, y 0.40) hanging straight down. (1) Chain: a tube or sweep of small link bars (alternating oriented chain and chainDark short rod or capsule links) bending smoothly over joints chain1, chain2, chain3 from y 0.40 down to y 0.24, with a small gold jump ring at the top that loops through the lug. (2) Pendant on the joint 'pendant': a lion head medallion of radius about 0.05 centred at (0.105, 0.22, -0.04), seen from the front or +Z with its disc facing +Z and thin in z (about 0.02 thick). It has a gold rim ring, an outer mane of 10 to 12 gold spikes or shaped blades in a goldDeep to goldPale root-to-tip gradient, an inner lionFace disc, two eyes (black with a small white highlight), a small nose triangle and a muzzle with a mouth line, two small ears, and a sapphire gem on the forehead. A tiny wing or feather pair sits at each side of the disc. A small gold bail connects to chain3. Everything must be in the flat colours gold, goldDeep, goldPale, lionFace, chain, chainDark, black, sapphire. Keep x within 0.055-0.155 and y within 0.16-0.41.
parts.attaches: The top ring meets the left crossguard lug at chainAnchor. Joints chain1, chain2, chain3 and pendant run straight down along x about 0.105 and z -0.04, beside the grip (grip radius 0.03, so there is no collision).

calls.reasoning:
I'm picturing a Final Fantasy-style gunblade, like Squall's Revolver, standing upright on the floor with the blade pointing up, resting on its pommel or hilt.

I'm settling on overall proportions: roughly 0.34 wide, 1.5 tall, 0.48 deep, with the blade thin in x and broader in z. I'm laying out the y-axis sections from pommel through grip, guard/receiver with cylinder and hammer, up into the blade, planning to build each part as a separate mesh piece.

I'll keep joints modest—trigger, hammer, and cylinder hinges attached near the root weapon node. For the blade section, I'm allotting a separate "barrel" part running along the spine toward the tip, with a sight, muzzle, steel ridge, and glowing engravings, while the main blade carries the tapered fuller, edge bevel, spine step, notches, and rune carvings.

I'm planning five parts total: hilt, receiver, blade, barrel/ornament (covering spine barrel, muzzle, cartridge ejection, sights, glowing gem emblem, tassel), and a signature "lionCharm" piece—a chain with a lion pendant hanging off the guard near the grip, positioned so it doesn't overlap the hilt geometry.

Now I'm mapping out the precise coordinate geometry along the z-axis: the blade's spine-to-edge taper, the guard wings extending outward, the trigger guard and hammer positions, and where the barrel sits behind the spine, all anchored through the central x=0, z=0 axis.

Deciding to orient the cylinder axis along x so the chambers show on the side face, going with diameter 0.17 and width 0.08.

I'm sizing the crossguard wings modestly along x and planning gold wing-shaped guard pieces extending in z, then working out a compact color palette of steels, gunmetal, gold, and leather tones to keep under 24 colors.

Now I'm placing the key mount points: pommel at origin, grip top, receiver center, and the cylinder positioned slightly back and up near the receiver, with the blade base rising from the top of the receiver box around y 0.66-0.68.

Working out the trigger guard loop that curves beneath the receiver's rear, connecting the grip area to the back of the receiver with a downward-then-backward arc.

Now I'm placing the trigger and hammer pivots, then shifting focus to the hilt structure—pommel, grip with wrapping, collar rings, and an end gem that might need a glow effect.

Setting the overall hilt bounding box with a flat-bottomed pommel resting on the floor for stability. Then I'm working out the blade geometry, sizing it from base to tip and shaping its spine-and-edge profile in cross-section, plus planning a barrel overlay running along the blade like a gunblade design.

Now I'm dividing up ownership between parts: the barrel piece handles the muzzle, sights, spine ridge notches, gold inlay, and ejector, while the blade piece owns the body, bevel, fuller, runes, tip, edge highlights, and ricasso inset — keeping their details separate so nothing overlaps.

For the overall structure, I'm settling on five parts (hilt, receiver, blade, barrel, charm) with a weight budget totaling around 790 out of 900, and I'm working out the joint hierarchy starting from the root spine down through the trigger and hammer attachments with their positions and directions.

Now I'm figuring out the dangling chain elements, deciding to use a "tail" or "hinge" role for the chain segments and pendant, and laying out their positions so they cascade downward from the anchor point.

I'm checking that the lion-head pendant's bounding box fits within the charm's overall size and that the chain anchor sits properly on the crossguard wing.

I'm laying out the chain joints hanging down from the anchor to the pendant, checking radii stay within the grip's clearance. Then I'm sizing the receiver box and adjusting the trigger guard's lower bound so it doesn't overlap the receiver's minimum y.

Now I'm positioning the blade box relative to the receiver, making sure the blade root overlaps slightly into a collar mount rather than floating or clipping through the receiver's top edge.

I'm positioning the barrel from the receiver breech to the muzzle, checking it stays clear of the blade tip, then placing the hammer pivot at the rear of the receiver before starting on the hilt box dimensions.

Working through the hilt bounding box size based on blade and guard edges, then setting up the cylinder for the trigger mechanism—checking that the trigger pivot sits just outside the cylinder's circumference so there's no overlap.

For style, I'm leaning toward a gunblade reminiscent of the Lionheart: bright steel blade with an engraved fuller, gold filigree accents, a sapphire glow gem, and a lion pendant nod to Squall. Now I'm drafting the spec with clear conventions—blade lying in the YZ plane with thickness along x, edge facing +Z, left side as the +X face, and the cylinder visible from both sides—making sure each part's coordinates are spelled out precisely.
